paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this chapter. The world is covered in darkness, and Isaiah says so plainly: "darkness covers the earth, and thick darkness is over the peoples" (Isaiah 60:2). But the LORD doesn't leave it there. He says, "Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD rises upon you" (Isaiah 60:1). The light isn't something Zion makes up. It's the LORD's own glory, and it comes to her.

Now look at what that light does. Zion had been "forsaken and despised," and the LORD says He will make her "an everlasting pride, a joy from age to age" (Isaiah 60:15). Nations come, her children come home, and even people who once reviled her fall facedown and call her "the City of the LORD" (Isaiah 60:14). I know a little about being forgotten, and I'm telling you, it's NOT the end of the story when the LORD is the one writing it! The One who strikes in anger also shows mercy, and He says so Himself (Isaiah 60:10).

And the best part is where the light comes from. The sun and the moon fade out, because "the LORD will be your everlasting light" (Isaiah 60:19). All of it happens "so that I may be glorified" (Isaiah 60:21), and He says, "in its time I will accomplish it quickly" (Isaiah 60:22). So, baker, you can stay hopeful on the dark days, because the light is coming from Him, not from you. And that's why I keep my ovens ready.
